Versico Single-Ply Systems in Winston-Salem Roof Specifications

Versico manufactures TPO, PVC, and EPDM single-ply membrane systems along with insulation and accessory products that appear in commercial roof specifications we prepare for buildings across the area. We reference Versico's current technical documentation directly when a project calls for its product line, the same approach we take with any manufacturer named in a specification.

Product range and building fit

Versico's single-ply catalog spans the same broad membrane categories as other major manufacturers, giving us flexibility to match the appropriate membrane chemistry, thickness, and color to a building's specific rooftop traffic, exposure, and reflectivity requirements rather than being limited to a single product family. We assess each building's roof condition and use before selecting which Versico product line applies.

Insulation and cover board products from Versico are frequently specified alongside its membrane to keep the assembly within a single manufacturer's tested system, generally a requirement for full-system warranty eligibility rather than an optional consideration left to contractor discretion.

Specification and submittal process

A Versico-based specification names the exact membrane product, thickness, reinforcement, and attachment method, built from the manufacturer's current technical bulletins rather than general product familiarity. We confirm current documentation before finalizing any specification, since approved components and published details can change between literature updates.

Procurement teams reviewing bids naming Versico materials should request the specific product data sheet referenced in the proposal, confirming exact membrane thickness and reinforcement rather than assuming uniformity across a manufacturer's broader product catalog.

Warranty program structure

Versico's warranty programs, like those of comparable manufacturers, generally require installation by contractors meeting program standards and documentation of installed components at project completion. We do not represent a specific certification tier or program status without factual basis, and we recommend owners verify warranty terms directly with Versico rather than relying on contractor claims alone.

Warranty length and scope vary by system type, thickness, and program tier selected for a specific project, and those terms should be confirmed in writing before warranty coverage is used as a point of comparison between competing bids.

  • Current technical bulletins referenced for every Versico specification.
  • Membrane chemistry and thickness matched to actual building traffic and exposure conditions.
  • Insulation and cover board kept within the manufacturer's tested assembly for warranty eligibility.
  • Warranty program terms confirmed directly with the manufacturer in writing.
  • Bid comparisons checked to confirm equivalent product and thickness across competing contractors.

Piedmont field conditions and Versico systems

Hot-air welding on Versico TPO and PVC membrane requires the same attention to Piedmont summer dew point as any single-ply system, narrowing the practical installation window on humid mornings. Wind uplift ratings published for Versico systems need to be matched against each building's actual exposure category and parapet height rather than applied as a generic number across dissimilar roof shapes.

For re-cover projects over aging built-up or EPDM roofs common on older industrial buildings in the area, Versico's published guidance on substrate moisture verification informs our approach before any re-cover is proposed to an owner.

Rooftop traffic and thickness selection within the Versico line

Versico's TPO product range includes multiple thickness options, and the same traffic-based logic that governs any manufacturer's membrane thickness applies here: buildings with frequent rooftop mechanical service or equipment access justify a heavier specification, while low-traffic roofs are usually well served by a lighter thickness at a lower material cost. We review the actual mechanical service schedule for the building before recommending a specific Versico thickness rather than defaulting to a mid-range option out of habit.

Where a building's rooftop equipment count or access pattern has changed since a prior roof was installed, that change should factor into the next Versico specification, since a roof designed for occasional service may need reinforcement or a thicker membrane if equipment traffic has since increased.

Documentation practices

We provide owners with the specific Versico product data sheets referenced in a specification, giving procurement teams the manufacturer's own documentation to verify independently rather than a contractor summary alone. This keeps the specification traceable to source material throughout the bidding and installation process.

Any field adjustment to a standard Versico detail, required by existing building conditions, gets documented and, where warranty implications exist, communicated to the manufacturer's program representative rather than handled informally on site.

We also keep a copy of every Versico data sheet referenced on a given project inside the closeout file itself, not only in a separate procurement folder, so a facilities manager years later can find the exact specification without tracking down the original contractor or bid documents.

Questions about Versico roofing systems

What membrane types does Versico manufacture?

Versico manufactures TPO, PVC, and EPDM single-ply membrane systems along with related insulation and accessory products.

Does a Versico specification guarantee a specific warranty length?

No. Warranty terms depend on the specific product, thickness, and program tier selected, which should be confirmed directly with the manufacturer.

Can insulation from another manufacturer be paired with Versico membrane?

Full-system warranty programs generally require components from within the manufacturer's tested assembly, and substituting other brands can affect warranty standing.

How does Piedmont humidity affect Versico membrane installation?

Hot-air welding requires a dry surface, and summer dew point conditions can delay morning starts on humid days.

Do you hold a specific certification level with Versico?

We work from the manufacturer's current technical documentation for each project and recommend owners confirm any specific program standing directly with the manufacturer.
